claim_traces.claim_text: "mRNA COVID-19 vaccines alter or permanently change human DNA."
reasoning_steps: The claim that mRNA COVID-19 vaccines alter or permanently change human DNA is scientifically false

According to global health agencies (including the CDC, WHO, and NIH) and molecular biology consensus, mRNA from the vaccines delivers instructions to the cytoplasm of host cells to synthesize the harmless viral spike protein, triggering an immune response
The mRNA never enters the cell nucleus, where human DNA resides, and the body rapidly breaks down and eliminates the mRNA within days
Furthermore, human cells lack the biochemical mechanisms (such as reverse transcriptase and integrase) required to convert mRNA into DNA and integrate it into the human genome.

Neuroimaging techniques such as fMRI and PET scans demonstrate that virtually all parts of the brain are active and have known functions, even during sleep or simple tasks [1, 4, 5]

Furthermore, neuroscientists emphasize that any genuinely unused or dormant brain tissue would degenerate or atrophy, and damage to even minute areas of the brain typically causes measurable cognitive or physical impairment [2, 3, 4]
Scientific consensus universally rejects the idea that 90% of the brain remains dormant.

claim_traces.claim_text: "Napoleon Bonaparte was unusually short — around 5 feet 2 inches tall."
reasoning_steps: The claim that Napoleon Bonaparte was unusually short and stood around 5 feet 2 inches tall is a widespread historical myth
At his death, Napoleon was recorded as measuring 5 feet 2 inches in pre-metric French units (pieds and pouces)

Because French inches were longer than British inches (each French inch being about 2.71 cm compared to the British inch of 2.54 cm), his actual height was approximately 5 feet 6 inches to 5 feet 7 inches (roughly 168–170 cm)
For an early 19th-century French male, this was average or even slightly above average height
The enduring perception of him being miniature stems from unit conversion confusion and British wartime propaganda (such as caricatures by James Gillray).
